annotations.title: Check a claimed model retirement date against the register

description: Is this right? Check a claim about a model id — its shutdown date, its lifecycle status, the replacement it was given — against the provider's own record instead of trusting it. Says whether the claim equals a stored value, appears only in the verbatim quote, or differs (and then what the record says instead). A model retirement date recalled from memory is exactly the kind of confident wrong answer that leaves a config pinned to something that stopped answering.

claimed_value.description: The value to check, exactly as claimed, e.g. "Terminated" or "2026-10-29".

field.description: Which field the claim is about, if you know it. Without it, every stored field of the record is checked.

model_id.description: The model id the claim is about, matched the same way model_status matches it. Where more than one record holds the id, narrow with `provider` or `record_id` — the check is refused rather than run against whichever came first.

provider.description: Optional case-insensitive substring of the provider name, to pick which host's record the claim is checked against.

record_id.description: Optional. The exact record to check against, as model_status returns it in record_id. Settles the case where one provider holds the same id twice (AWS Bedrock publishes two schedules for claude-3-haiku, one per region group).

name: verify_quote

also_reported.description: Values for this record reported by a SECOND source, each with its own source_url and source_quote. Cite these to the page they name, never to the record's primary source.

record_url.description: This record's own page on referencesource.org.

source_quote.description: Verbatim text from that page containing the value.

source_url.description: The page the value was read from.

under_review.description: PRESENT ONLY when a re-reading of this record's own source page states a different value from the one published here. Each named field's value is unsettled and must be cited as disputed, not as the publisher's current position. Absent means no correction is on file for this record — it is never returned empty.

reported_on.description: The date we re-read the page.

reported_value_found_in_that_quote.description: Whether the NEW value was found verbatim inside the new quote. False means the re-reading is not itself quote-confirmed.

verdict.description: matches_record: the claim equals a stored value (match.match_type says how exactly). matches_quote: it appears in the verbatim source quote but is not a stored value. differs: the record was found and says something else — stored_values shows what. not_found: the record was not located, which says nothing about whether the claim is true.
